details.description: FireFunction-v2 is an open-weights function-calling model built by Fireworks AI on top of Meta's Llama 3 70B Instruct, released June 17, 2024. It is tuned for real-world agentic use -- multi-turn conversation, instruction following, and parallel function calling -- rather than narrowly overfitting to function-calling benchmarks, so it also keeps much of Llama 3's general chat ability. Fireworks reports it is competitive with GPT-4o on a combined function-calling benchmark medley (0.81 vs 0.80) and reliably handles up to 30 function specifications in a single call.
advantages: Fireworks reports FireFunction-v2 handles up to 30 function specifications reliably in one call, versus about 5 for FireFunction-v1.
Scores 0.81 on Fireworks' combined function-calling benchmark medley (Gorilla, Nexus, MT-Bench), close to GPT-4o's 0.80, per the launch post.
Retains general chat and instruction-following ability from its Llama 3 70B Instruct base, scoring 0.84 on MT-Bench versus the base model's 0.89.
Supports parallel function calling (calling more than one function from a single query), which Fireworks says FireFunction-v1 often failed at.
disadvantages: Not optimized for more than 100 function specifications or for nested function calling, per its Hugging Face model card.
MT-Bench score of 0.84 trails GPT-4o's 0.93 and its own Llama 3 70B Instruct base's 0.89, indicating a general-chat quality gap versus those models.
Limited to an 8K-token context window, inherited from its Llama 3 70B Instruct base.
use_cases: Chat assistants that mix ordinary conversation with function/tool calls.
Parallel function calling across multiple APIs within a single turn.
Routing and decision-making applications that select among many available functions.
Structured information extraction from natural-language input.

sources.title: Firefunction-v2: Function calling capability on par with GPT4o at 2.5x the speed and 10% of the cost
FireFunction V2 API & Playground | Fireworks AI

notes: Catalog facts list max_input/output tokens as 8192, matching Fireworks' stated 8K context window inherited from the Llama 3 70B Instruct base. The Hugging Face model card gives a slightly different summary metric (average 0.82 for FireFunction-v2 vs GPT-4o's 0.80) than the launch blog post's medley average (0.81 vs 0.80); I used the launch post's more detailed per-benchmark table as the primary source for the evaluations listed here.
